test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence is in indirect speech. Choose the option that conveys it in direct speech.

He said that he had been waiting there for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.

options.text: He said, "I have been waiting here since two hours before the gates opened."
He said, "I waited here two hours before gates opened."
He said, 'I was waiting here for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.
He said, "I had waiting there before the gates opened."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in indirect speech, which describes a past event with the reporting verb in the past tense ("said").
 
• The phrase "he had been waiting there for more than two hours before the gates finally opened" indicates the use of past perfect continuous tense.
 
• In direct speech, past perfect continuous tense is typically converted to past continuous when quoting the exact words spoken.
 
• Option 3 correctly converts the sentence into direct speech: **'I was waiting here for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.'**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, 'I was waiting here for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I have been waiting here since two hours before the gates opened." – This is incorrect because "have been waiting" is present perfect continuous, which does not match the past context.
 
• **Option 2:** "I waited here two hours before gates opened." – This is incorrect as it uses simple past tense, which does not convey the continuous action described in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** "I had waiting there before the gates opened." – This is grammatically incorrect as "had waiting" is an incorrect verb form.
 
• **Option 3:** "I was waiting here for more than two hours before the gates finally opened." – This is the correct conversion as it uses past continuous tense to represent the original meaning accurately.
